Joburg Surgical Healing Hope

By: Floris Kotze | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
In the leafy suburbs of Johannesburg, amidst a backdrop of pain and uncertainty, a beacon of hope rises – the Johannesburg Surgical Hospital, where lives are transformed and the future of healthcare

Unique Selling Point:
In 'Healing Hope: Johannesburg Surgical Hospital,' witness the inspiring journey of a cutting-edge medical facility that defies the odds to bring world-class healthcare to South Africa. Against the backdrop of a struggling healthcare system, Carte Blanche delves into the determination of a group of dedicated doctors who create a legacy of healing, innovation, and hope within the heart of Johannesburg.

Summary:
We takea viewers on a gripping medical journey into the heart of South Africa's healthcare challenges. Amidst a backdrop of four colliding epidemics and a struggling public healthcare system, a group of visionary doctors takes matters into their own hands. They establish the Johannesburg Surgical Hospital, a state-of-the-art facility funded and run by the very doctors who work there.

We showcase the hospital's inspiring mission to provide the best care money can buy and its commitment to training a new generation of specialists. Viewers follow the emotional journey of a patient, Maria Kyriacou, whose life-changing surgery becomes a symbol of the hospital's dedication to making a difference.

Through interviews with the hospital's founder, Dr. Pieter Strobos, and its manager, Alex Daneel, reveals the challenges they faced in establishing this world-class facility. Despite these obstacles, the hospital stands as a testament to innovation and resilience in the face of adversity.

'Healing Hope' offers an inside look at the hospital's operations, its dedication to affordability, and its vision for positive change in South Africa's healthcare sector. Dr. Strobos's philosophy of planting seeds for a better future resonates as the documentary concludes with Maria's successful recovery, leaving viewers inspired by the transformative power of healthcare and hope.

Script:


Opening:
Hospital and Podcasts / Upsounds / News
UPSOUNDS:
“South Africa's public health care system needs urgent government intervention.”
“shortage of medicine, shortage of staff, it's a chronic problem. As I've said, it's a consequence of the underfunding,”
“South Africa is reportedly facing a talent flight in doctors and medical professionals because of the National Health Insurance Scheme. “

Opening Maria
My name is Maria. I have been suffering with shoulder pain for over 10 years. And for me the only option now is surgery.
I am not going to lie, I am slightly freaked out, and scared. But I am ready for this.

Opening Link:
In the heart of bustling suburbia stands Johannesburg Surgical Hospital, a cutting edge health hub funded by the very specialists working here. Granted an all access pass, we're about to follow Maria as she gets her shoulder surgery.

VO1:
Maria has been diagnosed with an impingement, a tendon rubbing on her shoulder blade. We are on our way to meet the surgeon who will lead the operation, Doctor Jaco Strobos. Affectionately known as, Dr Shoulder.
He is not only an Orthopaedic specialist, but also the mastermind behind this hospital.
Intrigued with the fact that he has his own hospital, I decided to join him at his home, to find out more about him.

DR Strobos:
My uncle had a big role in my life and decision making because he was an engineer and I liked the way he was doing things and he was like a role model for me. So that made me ask him the question, what do I do? And he says, study medicine. And I'm a little bit compulsive probably. I said, OK, then I will become a doctor.

VO2:
In private practice for over 20 years, he's always had big dreams… and one dream in particular…

Dr Strobos
I always wanted to do a hospital where the doctors can make the choices of what they want.
I wanted to give the people that are working with me something that they can leave for their children as well.




VO3:
Bureaucracy and red tape meant he waited years to get a licence to build a hospital - by 2018, the dream came into reach - with a licence in hand, he just needed some funds.

LINK:
What sets Johannesburg Surgical Hospital apart is that it is owned and run by the doctors. Most specialists here have taken their destiny into their own hands and invested their own money into the project. How much you ask? Well, let's just say it's substantial.

VO4
He needed an enormous R920 million for the development. The bank approved a loan but on one condition, he had to raise significant deposits.
So he approached his colleagues and sold them his lifelong dream.
They managed to raise R320 million!
This meant that the hospital was private, steering clear of public listing and enabling doctors to prioritise patients over profit.

Prof Jay
People look at private hospitals where doctors have a financial input into it.
It's a frowned upon concept.

VO5
Professor Jay Pillai is the Academic Head of Vascular Surgery at Wits University - he practises in private, public and academic sectors.

Prof Jay
The initiation of this has to be policy soundproof. And by that I mean, when a doctor buys a share in a hospital, there's always a chance of perversity, there's always a chance of competition, tribunal, investigations, and there's always vulnerability to the doctor.
So if you create policies in a new hospital then that policy can be learned by other new hospitals.

Dr Strobos
Nobody could get more than 5% share. There is not one guy that owns this thing. Everybody is at the same level. the day I stopping to work at the hospital, my 5% shares, I have to sell it. And I have to sell it to a youngster that I have trained and to take over from me.
And the reason for that is simple. You get a hospital where the guys get older, they keep their shares, but youngsters can't come in to renew it and then the business goes down.






VOXIES:

Dr Bloy
There's always a lot of doom and gloom in our country, but at least if you can create these pockets of excellence and bright lights, at least it makes it all worthwhile for all of us and for our patients in particular.

Dr Shohan
we've got world-class specialists here. So we can offer patients the best that they would get anywhere in the world.

Maria:
Pray for me!

VO6
Meanwhile our patient, Maria, is just about ready for theatre.

Dr Strobos:
Where is our Music?

VO7
If you are squeamish, I’d suggest you look away now…
Maria’s operation is about to start.

Dr Strobos:
So this is my posterior portal.
So here we are going inside the shoulder now.
This is like music. You have to create miracle music that makes people's lives better.
There is a little bit of fluff, I am cleaning it.
If I walk into theatre, I'm putting on the surgeon's cloak.(...) Then I want things to be done in a certain way.
This is the shoulder bone. The tip of the shoulder is the scapula. It's the acromion.(...) And I'm cleaning it now, like you can see,
The amazing thing walking into a theatre where I have the right equipment, the staff now understands what I want to achieve, and the team is getting together.
I remember watching other surgeons doing arthroscopic surgery.
And eventually, when you do it yourself, that feeling of you can't believe it that you're actually doing those things. It's like you want to do this.(...) Wake up.
And now we're just going to repair the wounds. We have finished.





Dr Strobos:
When I pick up the knife, I think I want to be doing it 100% right.
When I get to other things, then we enjoy life. I like to enjoy life.

VO:8
And he certainly does just that! Dr Strobos showed me some of his handy-work around the house.
From bells salvaged from shipwrecks to building his own brewery!

Upsound:
Claire: I am seeing trains, the brewery, woodwork, why do all of these things?
Dr: I think I want to live life to the fullest. Eventually you will sit on your deathbed and say, "I did want to do this and this and this and this. I never want to say that. I want to do everything to the fullest."

LINK:
It's hard to be here and not think of the millions of South Africans who can't access quality health care. This is where the National Health Insurance comes in.

UPSOUND:
Public hospitals are plagued by,corruption.(...)
So if you don't introduce the NHI, that improvement will never happen. But you can't introduce it with a broken system…

VO9
There is much debate about the National HEALTH Insurance Bill, it aims for universal health coverage - regardless of income, granting equal access to healthcare. However, concerns arise as the government gains control of a substantial sum, around R500 BILLION. Past corruption and mismanagement have eroded trust in the government's administration of the NHI, especially when viable alternatives are available.

Prof Jay
Perhaps we should state at the inception that a different healthcare system is mandatory and necessary. And one of them are what we call PPPs, the public-private partnerships.
If we start saying that we have many, many private hospitals with limited occupancy, can we create policy to get some of those hospital beds in some economically feasible fashion to be used by the state.

Closing Link:
Mavericks at Dr. Strobos are exactly what we need. If you think about it, the easier thing would have been to complain about the state of healthcare in this country, pack up and leave. But - he decided to stay and build something that will last generations.

Dr Strobos:
I want to be a proud South African. I want to do something for South Africa.
I want to create things that I have the the passion for and I want the government to help private individuals, private companies, private people that wants to make a difference. I want that to happen in South Africa. That's my dream for South Africa.

Closing Maria Out

Upsound:
we hide behind the third world issue. We need to actually take our value
money where we want it to be and develop this country where
Could Joburg's newest hospital give patients the worldclass treatment they deserve?

21” Promo 3
Upsound: I want to live life to the fullest. We have one chance.
VO: A team of super specialists with a mission to make a difference. Discover why this new medical centre in Johannesburg is a true game changer.
